markdown:
Every semester a student tells me that theory kills the music. the complaint is sincere, and it is wrong. Nobody says that grammar kills the novel, or that knowing what a cadence is spoils the end of a Beethoven sonata.

What students actually resent is being asked to learn the basic fundamentals before they are allowed to be interesting. I understand the feeling. But the composers they admire learned the same scales, and most of them learned them earlier and harder.

Theory is a vocabulary for hearing. You can play without it, as you can speak without knowing what a verb is, but you will have a harder time saying what you mean.
